title: Auto-start queue for coding agent runs
summary: Adds a per-project agent run queue (new REQ, story STORY-0014, 3 tasks, 2 evals). It is off by default, its concurrency limit defaults to 2, and it auto-starts todo tasks whose story's requirements are all approved. REQ-0051 AC1 and REQ-0052 AC4 are updated to cover queued runs.
rationale: The product owner wants approved work to start in Claude Code without a click per task. Decisions: a task is eligible when every requirement linked to its story is approved (stories have no approval status). The concurrency limit is configurable per project, default 2. The queue is off by default, and the user who turns it on is the accountable starting user of every queued run.

data.title: Agent run queue
data.statement: The system shall, while a project's agent queue is on, automatically start a coding agent run for each eligible todo task, with at most the project's configured number of concurrent runs (default 2).
data.rationale: Lets approved work start in Claude Code without a click per task, while bounding machine load and keeping each run attributable to a user.

acceptance_criteria.text: The queue is off for every project by default; turning it on or off is a per-project setting, requires a confirmation showing the number of eligible tasks, and records the user and time

A task is eligible only if its status is todo, every requirement linked to its story has status approved, every task in its depends_on is done, and its story's component has a path; no other task is started
The number of concurrent runs per project never exceeds the configured limit (integer 1 to 8, default 2); when a run ends, the next eligible task in ascending task id order starts within 30 s
A queued run uses the same worktree, branch, brief and progress view as a UI-started run (REQ-0051 AC2 to AC5) and moves the task to in-progress when it starts
A run that fails or is cancelled is not restarted by the queue; turning the queue off starts 0 new runs and leaves active runs running
The tasks view shows the queue state (on/off, enabling user), the running tasks and the waiting eligible tasks in start order

ops.reason: New capability requested by product owner

acceptance_criteria.text: For a run started from the UI, a confirmation dialog shows the component path, the branch name reqforge/TASK-NNNN and the full brief, and nothing runs until the user confirms; runs started by the agent queue are authorised by the user who turned the queue on
The agent runs via the local claude CLI in a git worktree of the component on branch reqforge/TASK-NNNN
The brief contains the task description and done_when, the story narrative, each linked requirement statement and acceptance criteria, and the trace tag convention
Agent progress streams to the task drawer and the user can cancel the run
When the run ends, the task shows its branch, commits and exit status, and the task status is never set to done automatically
Start with agent is disabled, with the reason shown, when the story has no component, the component has no path, or any task in depends_on is not done

ops.reason: AC1 required per-run confirmation, which conflicts with queued runs; scope it to UI-started runs

acceptance_criteria.text: An agent run makes 0 commits or pushes to the default branch and pushes only to reqforge/TASK-* branches
An agent run writes 0 files outside its worktree, including the requirements repository
The coding agent has 0 reqforge record-write or changeset-apply tools
Every run is logged with task id, starting user (for queued runs, the user who turned the queue on), whether it was queued, start and end time, branch and exit status

ops.reason: Keep audit trail accountable for queued runs

stories: STORY-0013's scope is unchanged except for the AC wording below; the queue reuses its agent launcher, so STORY-0014 can't ship before TASK-0028.
code: No code exists yet for REQ-0051, REQ-0052 or the queue, so no trace tags need updating.
New test files to create: server/tests/agent_queue.rs and web/e2e/suites/agent-queue.js (registered in run.mjs).

Existing tests planned for STORY-0013 (agent-start e2e for REQ-0051#AC1, agent_sandbox for REQ-0052#AC4) must assert the new wording: queued runs skip the dialog, and the run log records the queued flag and the enabling user.
evals: 2 new evals: STORY-0014/E1 (integration) and E2 (e2e). STORY-0013/E2 and E3 keep the same coverage refs but test the reworded AC1 and AC4.
risks: Automatic runs execute code-editing agents without per-run review. This is mitigated by off-by-default, the REQ-0052 sandbox (main branch untouched, worktree-only writes) and an accountable enabling user.
Nothing can be queued until code components with paths are configured (none today) and REQ-0049 depends_on exists.
New ids REQ-0053, STORY-0014 and TASK-0030 to TASK-0032 reuse ids of the duplicates deleted in CS-0007; git history before CS-0007 refers to different records.
